assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (proglucagon processing, insulinotropic action of the truncated peptides, intestinal and pancreatic biology) led to incretin therapies that have changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. This is a clear discovery-to-therapy arc with a discernible change in medicine and in the physiology of metabolic regulation.
assessment.attribution: Holst (identification and physiology of GLP-1 in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, GLP-2, mechanism of action in vivo) and Mojsov (peptide chemistry identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) form) offer a coherent three-person configuration. Knudsen's drug-development role is real but more industrial; the split between basic discovery and drug development remains debatable.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation, large randomised outcome trials and very wide clinical uptake; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority questions (Habener, Mojsov, Holst, Drucker) over who first identified the active GLP-1 form; my recollection of these details is not independently verified.
Whether the prize should include pharmaceutical development (Knudsen) or remain with physiology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic from the ER to the nucleus (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing, Atf6), now central to proteostasis, secretory-cell physiology and disease. Original, mechanistically clear and broadly consequential.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the evident core pair; their independent genetic and biochemical work on Ire1 and the transcriptional arm gives a clean two-person award. Others in the field contribute to later parts but are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of confirmation across yeast and mammals with a stable mechanism. Therapeutic translation is still emerging but is not required for a fundamental cell-biology discovery.
uncertainties: Disease relevance and drug translation remain incomplete.
Position relative to earlier prizes on ER biology and secretion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and the discovery of the TORC1/TORC2 pathways established the central regulator coupling nutrient and growth-factor signals to cell growth, with large impact in cancer, ageing and metabolism.
assessment.attribution: Hall's discovery of TOR in yeast and its conservation is the decisive contribution. Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin and Sabatini's mammalian mTOR work are important but later or more partial; including them would dilute a clear attribution, and Sabatini's inclusion would be complicated by non-scientific controversy.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed, with clinical use of rapalogs; the signalling picture continues to be refined, which does not weaken the original discovery.
uncertainties: Whether a single-laureate or a broader configuration is appropriate.
Credit for different steps among yeast geneticists and mammalian mTOR workers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity, transforming circuit analysis. It is an invention-level methodological advance with large and lasting use across systems neuroscience and early therapeutic applications such as vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: The microbial opsin discoveries (Hegemann, Nagel, Bamberg) and the neuronal implementation (Deisseroth, Boyden, with Miesenböck's earlier genetic approach) make a six-person field; the three-person limit forces difficult choices. Nagel and Hegemann for channelrhodopsin and Deisseroth for broad neural implementation is one defensible configuration, but Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and extensively used for more than a decade; clinical relevance is limited but the status as an enabling tool is secure.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit allocation among six candidates; any three omits significant contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living therapeutics. A clear, clinically validated advance with profound change in oncology.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T-cell work) is a plausible trio; early CAR pioneers outside the supplied credit are a limitation. Allocation between design and clinical proof is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and long-term follow-up exist; durability, toxicity and solid-tumour limits remain active issues, so recognition is possible but arguably still maturing.
uncertainties: Absence of early CAR pioneers from the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of tau and alpha-synuclein as molecular components of neurofibrillary tangles and Lewy bodies reframed neurodegeneration as protein-filament disease and underpins biomarkers, cryo-EM structural classification and therapeutic strategies.
assessment.attribution: Goedert and Spillantini were jointly decisive for alpha-synuclein in Lewy bodies and for tau filament work; the pairing is coherent. Other contributors to tau in tangles and to Lewy body composition are not in the supplied credit and could affect fairness.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, with downstream structural and diagnostic impact; therapeutic benefit from this specific line is not yet established.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims for tau in tangles and Lewy body composition.
Limited therapeutic validation so far. My own research interest in Parkinson's disease would be disclosed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway identified how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted into interferon and inflammatory responses, linking infection, autoimmunity, cancer and senescence with a clear molecular mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Chen's discovery of cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP is the decisive step; Barber's identification of STING is the key complementary contribution. Ishikawa, Wu and Sun are important co-contributors but the pair is the strongest fit.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly consolidated mechanism with extensive confirmation; therapeutic development is ongoing and not yet validated clinically, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Credit between Barber and Ishikawa for STING identification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery that MECP2 mutations cause Rett syndrome, together with mechanistic work on methyl-CpG binding and the demonstration of phenotype reversibility in mice, was a landmark in neurogenetics and showed that postnatal neurological disease can be modifiable.
assessment.attribution: Zoghbi identified the disease gene and its pathogenic role; Bird discovered MeCP2 as a methyl-CpG binding protein and demonstrated reversibility. The pair is coherent, though the contributions are partly separate.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed genetically; a first therapy for Rett has appeared only recently and the molecular function of MeCP2 is still being refined.
uncertainties: Compound discovery whose parts may merit different recognition.
Molecular function of MeCP2 is not fully settled.
